_doc: Settings only the data pipeline reads (Python scripts and workflows); the app never imports this file. See src/cities/README.md.

imdGrid.note: Nearest valid land grid point to Chennai (coastal cells classified as ocean by IMD)

ingres._note: Chennai extends the WRIS series in public/data/gwr-blocks.json. Its units are matched by AREA, never by name: in the 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 editions IN-GRES labels Chennai's taluks one place down the alphabet from Madhavaram on (the 7,068 ha unit, Chennai's largest, is labelled PURASAIVAKKAM; 'KOLATHUR' stands in for Velachery), while 2025-26 labels the same areas by their true names. The WRIS series already carries the true names, so those editions re-run here with no change. 2025-26 is left out: it assesses 17 units (Kolathur, 700 ha, carved out of Ayanavaram; Thiruvottiyur 285 ha smaller) and the 16 polygons here are the old set.

_notes.end_year_labels: The WRIS years before it are labelled by end year (2020, 2022), so the IN-GRES editions are too; a mixed "2022, 2022-23" reads as a repeat.
_notes.unit_areas: area.total.totalArea (ha, rounded) -> the block name the series uses.

elevationBands._note: Chennai is a coastal alluvial plain - almost everything sits under 20 m, so the low bands are cut finer than Mumbai's.
